title: Favicon and web app icons
learningObjectives: Explain favicon and web app icons and apply accurate document metadata or print structure.

understand.concept: A favicon identifies a site in browser tabs, bookmarks, and other browser interfaces. A page can link to icon files using rel=icon, and web app manifests can define application icons for installation or launch surfaces. Different sizes and formats may be supplied.
understand.whyItMatters: Icons should be legible at small sizes and available at appropriate paths. Keep the favicon and manifest icons consistent with the product identity and avoid relying on a single large image for every context.
understand.analogy: A favicon is a small visual label that helps users recognise the site among many open tabs.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser metadata and search/social platform processing are governed by their respective specifications and policies.

explain.narrative: The document declares an SVG favicon, a PNG fallback, and a web app manifest.

examples.code: <head><link rel='icon' href='/favicon.svg' type='image/svg+xml'><link rel='icon' href='/favicon-32.png' sizes='32x32' type='image/png'><link rel='manifest' href='/manifest.webmanifest'></head>
examples.explanation: The document declares an SVG favicon, a PNG fallback, and a web app manifest.
examples.expectedOutput: A valid HTML head or print-style example demonstrating the topic.

practise.guidedTask: Create a favicon link set and verify the referenced files exist. Check the manifest icon declarations and test small-size legibility.
practise.independentTask: Prepare metadata or print styles for a sample course page. Verify paths, content accuracy, language declarations, and the print result.
hints: Use absolute URLs where metadata requires them.
Do not invent structured data claims.
Keep the visible page consistent with metadata.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Favicon and web app icons</title></head><body>
<head><link rel='icon' href='/favicon.svg' type='image/svg+xml'><link rel='icon' href='/favicon-32.png' sizes='32x32' type='image/png'><link rel='manifest' href='/manifest.webmanifest'></head>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which rel value commonly identifies a favicon link?
questions.explanation: rel=icon identifies a site icon resource.

questions.prompt: What is the most important rule for page metadata?
options: It must accurately describe the actual page
It should contain as many keywords as possible
It can claim features not present on the page
questions.answer: It must accurately describe the actual page
questions.explanation: Metadata should be accurate, consistent, and not misleading.
